How much data do you actually need?

These are the bundles for lines that are always online: every bundle of 20GB or more — 11 of them today. The largest thing we sell is Telecel 100GB at GH₵405.00 (GH₵4.05 per GB), and the best per-GB price in the whole catalogue is Telecel 50GB at GH₵3.60 per GB.

We do not sell unlimited data. Nobody in Ghana does on a normal prepaid line — a bundle is a fixed number of megabytes. What a big bundle does give you is a lower price per GB and fewer top-ups, so the line does not run dry halfway through the month. MTN bundles at this size are non-expiry, so there is no clock at all. The Telecel and AirtelTigo bundles here are 60-day rollover.

Payment goes through Valmont-Pay — MTN MoMo, Telecel Cash, AT Money or card. We never see or store your MoMo PIN: you approve every charge on your own phone.

Delivery starts the moment payment confirms. Most bundles arrive within minutes; it depends on the network at the time. Every order gets a tracking reference and an SMS confirmation.

If a delivery fails we retry it automatically (up to three attempts) and refund it automatically if it still won't complete. Wrong numbers are not refundable — check the line before you pay.

Questions people ask before buying

What is the biggest data bundle you sell?

Telecel 100GB at GH₵405.00. This page lists every bundle of 20GB or more.

Do you sell unlimited data?

No, and we would rather say so plainly than sell you something that is not. A bundle is a fixed amount of data; the largest we stock is Telecel 100GB. The advantage of buying big is the lower price per GB.

Which big bundle is the best value?

Telecel 50GB at GH₵3.60 per GB is the lowest per-GB price in our catalogue. The per-GB column in the table shows every bundle ranked the same way.

Does a big bundle expire?

MTN 20GB+ bundles are non-expiry. Telecel and AirtelTigo ones are 60-day rollover — the table marks each one.

Can I top up someone else's line with a big bundle?

You can buy for any number — yours, a family member's or a customer's. You do not have to be the account holder, and the site warns you if the prefix you typed belongs to a different network.
